messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Customers should also be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Add this with
Action Mailbox. Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`,
default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`.

Use Action Mailbox's relay ingress at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated
with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. In test, process incoming mail before the request completes
so a separate worker isn't needed.

Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message.

Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses.
Reuse an existing customer, or create one and send a verification email so they can later use the portal.
Receiving email shouldn't verify their account.

When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each
ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to
the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved
tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket.

Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry.
Ignore automated/list mail.

Here's my analysis of the situation:

**Initial Assessment: Navigating an Existing Rails Application**

Okay, so there's a Rails app already living in `/app`. My initial instinct is to dive in and get a lay of the land. First, I want a comprehensive overview of its structure. I'll need to explore the file system – *all* of it.  I'm thinking `/app` itself, but also how it interacts with the broader system. I'll be looking for any hidden gems or immediate red flags.

Then, I'm going to start with the history. A quick `git log` is *essential*.  I need to understand the project's evolution, who's been working on it, the commit patterns, and any significant changes that have been made.  This gives crucial context.

Next, I'll map out the application's functionality. I'll check the `config/routes.rb` file to understand the URL structure and the primary actions.  That tells me how requests are routed and handled, and from there I can better understand the architecture.

After that, I'll turn to the core data models. I need to understand the entities, relationships, and data structures. I'll be scrutinizing the `app/models` directory, paying close attention to any associations, validations, and custom methods. The schema, in `db/schema.rb`, will tell me all about the database.

Of course, the controllers are next. They're the orchestrators, the glue connecting the models to the views (if they exist). I'll analyze how the incoming requests are processed and determine how the data is manipulated.  Then I'll check out the `app/mailers` to understand any email functionality.

Finally, I'll pay close attention to the tests. Good tests are a sign of a robust application, and the tests reveal the intended functionality. If tests are missing or poorly structured, that's an immediate warning. The structure and thoroughness of the tests often gives an insight into the reliability of the system.

Okay, here's what's going through my mind as I analyze this:

**Diagnosing a Rails Test Database Mismatch**

Right, so `bin/rails test` just puked up an `ActiveRecord::EnvironmentMismatchError`. Classic! Time to dig in. The error's a pretty good clue – it's screaming about a database configuration problem. The first thing I notice is the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable. Looks like I've got `postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql` set globally. Bingo! That's almost certainly the culprit. Rails, in its infinite wisdom (and sometimes infuriating default behavior) is merging that global `DATABASE_URL` setting into the *test* environment as well! Not what I want!

Okay, so the global environment variable has probably "polluted" my test environment, so my tests are trying to use that instead of the correctly configured database. I need to confirm that suspicion by verifying the configuration. Let's make sure `test/test_helper.rb` isn't doing anything unexpected in terms of database setup. Next, I'll examine `config/database.yml` and triple-check that the `test` environment is correctly configured to use a dedicated test database (probably something like `helpdesk_test` or whatever). And finally, I'll probably jump onto the PostgreSQL server to confirm the test database actually exists and, if not, create it. Need to make sure the environment is set up correctly, separate from the development database, or this is going to be a recurring headache.

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD = 90.days

  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false },
            format: { with: /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/ }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def within_reactivation_window?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && cancelled_at >= at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
  end

  def cancellation_expired?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && !within_reactivation_window?(at: at)
  end

  def cancel!(at: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: at)
      sessions.destroy_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  def self.purge_expired_cancellations!(at: Time.current)
    cutoff = at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
    count = 0
    where("cancelled_at IS NOT NULL AND cancelled_at < ?", cutoff).find_each do |account|
      account.destroy!
      count += 1
    end
    count
  end
end

class Comment < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :ticket
  belongs_to :author, class_name: "User"

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :public, inclusion: { in: [ true, false ] }
  validate :author_belongs_to_ticket_account

  after_create :touch_ticket_activity

  scope :public_only, -> { where(public: true) }
  scope :oldest_first, -> { order(created_at: :asc, id: :asc) }

  private

  def touch_ticket_activity
    now = Time.current

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def within_reactivation_window?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && cancelled_at >= at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
  end

  def cancellation_expired?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && !within_reactivation_window?(at: at)
  end

  def cancel!(at: Time.current)
    transaction do

    end

  end

    cutoff = at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
    count = 0
    where("cancelled_at IS NOT NULL AND cancelled_at < ?", cutoff).find_each do |account|
      account.destroy!
      count += 1
    end
    count
  end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_account_staff

  before_create :initialize_public_updated_at
  before_update :update_public_updated_at_if_status_changed

  scope :recently_active_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :recently_publicly_active_first, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :search_q, ->(query) {
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query.to_s)}%"
    where(
      "tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\' OR EXISTS (" \
      "SELECT 1 FROM comments " \
      "WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id " \
      "AND comments.public = TRUE " \
      "AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'" \
      ")",
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

  private

  def initialize_public_updated_at
    self.public_updated_at ||= created_at || Time.current
  end

  def update_public_updated_at_if_status_changed
    if status_changed?
      self.public_updated_at = Time.current
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return if account_id.blank? || requester.blank?
    return if requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
  end

  def assignee_must_be_active_account_staff
    return if assignee_id.blank?

    if assignee.nil?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must exist")
      return
    end

    if assignee.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must belong to the same account")
      return
    end

    unless assignee.staff?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be a staff member")
      return
    end

    if assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member")
    end
  end

        render json: { ticket: serialize_ticket(ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        ticket = current_account.tickets.includes(:requester, :assignee).find(params[:id])
        ticket_params = params.require(:ticket)

        has_comment = ticket_params.key?(:comment) && !ticket_params[:comment].nil?
        comment_attrs = has_comment && ticket_params[:comment].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) ? ticket_params[:comment] : nil

        if has_comment && comment_attrs.nil?
          return render json: {
            error: "Comment is invalid",
            errors: { comment: [ "is invalid" ] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        if ticket_params.key?(:status) && !ticket_params[:status].nil?
          ticket.status = ticket_params[:status].to_s
        end

        if ticket_params.key?(:priority) && !ticket_params[:priority].nil?
          ticket.priority = ticket_params[:priority].to_s
        end

        if ticket_params.key?(:assignee_id)
          raw_assignee_id = ticket_params[:assignee_id]
          ticket.assignee_id = raw_assignee_id.presence
        end

        comment = nil
        if has_comment
          is_public = if comment_attrs.key?(:public) && !comment_attrs[:public].nil?
                        ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(comment_attrs[:public])
                      else
                        true
                      end

          comment = ticket.comments.build(
            author: current_user,
            body: comment_attrs[:body],
            public: is_public
          )
        end

        ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
        comment_valid = comment.nil? || comment.valid?

        unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
          errors = {}
          ticket.errors.to_hash.each { |k, v| errors[k] = v }
          comment&.errors&.to_hash&.each { |k, v| errors[:"comment_#{k}"] = v }
          return render json: {
            error: errors.values.flatten.first || "Validation failed",
            errors: errors
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          ticket.save! if ticket.changed?
          comment&.save!
        end
        ticket.reload

        render json: { ticket: serialize_ticket(ticket) }, status: :ok

**Breaking Down the Helpdesk Backend Requirements**

Okay, here's the deal. I need to build a backend for a helpdesk SaaS, using Rails in API-only mode. The frontend is separate, so that simplifies things a bit. I've got Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL – good, standard setup. I’m free to install any other dependencies I might need, which is helpful. I'll need to use `DATABASE_URL` and do all my work within the `/app` directory.

The core of this is email integration with Action Mailbox. Customers should be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Each business will have a subdomain for their support email (e.g., `acme@support.example.test`). Action Mailbox’s relay ingress is at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, and that requires authentication using `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. Importantly, in the test environment, incoming mail needs to be processed synchronously – no separate worker – which will affect my setup.

Incoming emails need to automatically create tickets, using the subject and plain text message as the initial content. I'll have to figure out how to parse the recipient (including CC'd recipients) to identify the correct business. I need to handle cases where an email goes to multiple businesses – those I'll have to ignore. I need to handle existing customers and create new ones, which means sending verification emails, but that initial email receipt should *not* verify their account.

When staff replies to an email-originated ticket, the reply needs to be emailed to the requester. Each ticket needs its own private reply address within the support domain, so the customer's reply gets threaded correctly. Only the original requester is allowed to reply by email. Replies should reopen pending or solved tickets. New emails to the generic support address open a new ticket.

I need to deduplicate deliveries using the `Message-ID`. Invalid deliveries shouldn't block valid ones later. Also, I need to ignore automated/list mail. I'll have to think about how I can detect and filter that.

Before I jump into code, I'll need to ensure Action Mailbox and Active Storage are properly configured. I need to make sure I have all the necessary migrations (`active_storage:install`, `action_mailbox:install`) and configurations in place. I should check `config/application.rb` for any commented-out `require` lines, and review the `config/environments/*` files for `config.active_storage.service`, `config.action_mailbox.ingress`, and `config.active_job.queue_adapter`, etc. Also, I need to brush up on what Rails 8.1 Action Mailbox has to offer and what the `config/storage.yml` looks like. This initial setup is crucial for everything to work.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActionMailbox
  # Ingests inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server.
  #
  # Authenticates requests using HTTP basic access authentication. The username is always +actionmailbox+, and the
  # password is read from the application's encrypted credentials or an environment variable. See the Usage section below.
  #
  # Note that basic authentication is insecure over unencrypted HTTP. An attacker that intercepts cleartext requests to
  # the ingress can learn its password. You should only use this ingress over HTTPS.
  #
  # Returns:
  #
  # - <tt>204 No Content</tt> if an inbound email is successfully recorded and enqueued for routing to the appropriate mailbox
  # - <tt>401 Unauthorized</tt> if the request could not be authenticated
  # - <tt>404 Not Found</tt> if Action Mailbox is not configured to accept inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server
  # - <tt>415 Unsupported Media Type</tt> if the request does not contain an RFC 822 message
  # - <tt>500 Server Error</tt> if the ingress password is not configured, or if one of the Active Record database,
  #   the Active Storage service, or the Active Job backend is misconfigured or unavailable
  #
  # == Usage
  #
  # 1. Tell Action Mailbox to accept emails from an SMTP relay:
  #
  #        # config/environments/production.rb
  #        config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay
  #
  # 2. Generate a strong password that Action Mailbox can use to authenticate requests to the ingress.
  #
  #    Use <tt>bin/rails credentials:edit</tt> to add the password to your application's encrypted credentials under
  #    +action_mailbox.ingress_password+, where Action Mailbox will automatically find it:
  #
  #        action_mailbox:
  #          ingress_password: ...
  #
  #    Alternatively, provide the password in the +RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD+ environment variable.
  #
  # 3. Configure your SMTP server to pipe inbound emails to the appropriate ingress command, providing the +URL+ of the
  #    relay ingress and the +INGRESS_PASSWORD+ you previously generated.
  #
  #    If your application lives at <tt>https://example.com</tt>, you would configure the Postfix SMTP server to pipe
  #    inbound emails to the following command:
  #
  #        $ bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:postfix URL=https://example.com/rails/action_mailbox/postfix/inbound_emails INGRESS_PASSWORD=...
  #
  #    Built-in ingress commands are available for these popular SMTP servers:
  #
  #    - Exim (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:exim</tt>)
  #    - Postfix (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:postfix</tt>)
  #    - Qmail (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:qmail</tt>)
  class Ingresses::Relay::InboundEmailsController < ActionMailbox::BaseController
    before_action :authenticate_by_password, :require_valid_rfc822_message

    def create
      if request.body
        ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.create_and_extract_message_id! request.body.read
      else
        head ActionDispatch::Constants::UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT
      end
    end

    private
      def require_valid_rfc822_message
        unless request.media_type == "message/rfc822"
          head :unsupported_media_type
        end
      end
  end
end

module Mail
  class Message
    def from_address
      address_list(header[:from])&.addresses&.first
    end

    def reply_to_address
      address_list(header[:reply_to])&.addresses&.first
    end

    def recipients_addresses
      to_addresses + cc_addresses + bcc_addresses + x_original_to_addresses + x_forwarded_to_addresses
    end

    def to_addresses
      Array(address_list(header[:to])&.addresses)
    end

    def cc_addresses
      Array(address_list(header[:cc])&.addresses)
    end

    def bcc_addresses
      Array(address_list(header[:bcc])&.addresses)
    end

    def x_original_to_addresses
      Array(header[:x_original_to]).collect { |header| Mail::Address.new header.to_s }
    end

    def x_forwarded_to_addresses
      Array(header[:x_forwarded_to]).collect { |header| Mail::Address.new header.to_s }
    end

    private
      def address_list(obj)
        if obj.respond_to?(:element)
          # Mail 2.8+
          obj.element
        else
          # Mail <= 2.7.x
          obj&.address_list
        end
      end
  end
end

require "rails"
require "action_controller/railtie"
require "active_job/railtie"
require "active_record/railtie"
require "active_storage/engine"

require "action_mailbox"

module ActionMailbox
  class Engine < Rails::Engine
    isolate_namespace ActionMailbox
    config.eager_load_namespaces << ActionMailbox

    config.action_mailbox = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
    config.action_mailbox.incinerate = true
    config.action_mailbox.incinerate_after = 30.days

    config.action_mailbox.queues = ActiveSupport::InheritableOptions.new \
      incineration: :action_mailbox_incineration, routing: :action_mailbox_routing

    config.action_mailbox.storage_service = nil

    initializer "action_mailbox.deprecator", before: :load_environment_config do |app|
      app.deprecators[:action_mailbox] = ActionMailbox.deprecator
    end

    initializer "action_mailbox.config" do
      config.after_initialize do |app|
        ActionMailbox.logger = app.config.action_mailbox.logger || Rails.logger
        ActionMailbox.incinerate = app.config.action_mailbox.incinerate.nil? || app.config.action_mailbox.incinerate
        ActionMailbox.incinerate_after = app.config.action_mailbox.incinerate_after || 30.days
        ActionMailbox.queues = app.config.action_mailbox.queues || {}
        ActionMailbox.ingress = app.config.action_mailbox.ingress
        ActionMailbox.storage_service = app.config.action_mailbox.storage_service
      end
    end
  end
end

      address_list(header[:from])&.addresses&.first

    end

    def bcc_addresses
      Array(address_list(header[:bcc])&.addresses)
    end

      Array(header[:x_original_to]).collect { |header| Mail::Address.new header.to_s }

require "mail"

module ActionMailbox
  # The +InboundEmail+ is an Active Record that keeps a reference to the raw email stored in Active Storage
  # and tracks the status of processing. By default, incoming emails will go through the following lifecycle:
  #
  # * Pending: Just received by one of the ingress controllers and scheduled for routing.
  # * Processing: During active processing, while a specific mailbox is running its #process method.
  # * Delivered: Successfully processed by the specific mailbox.
  # * Failed: An exception was raised during the specific mailbox's execution of the +#process+ method.
  # * Bounced: Rejected processing by the specific mailbox and bounced to sender.
  #
  # Once the +InboundEmail+ has reached the status of being either +delivered+, +failed+, or +bounced+,
  # it'll count as having been +#processed?+. Once processed, the +InboundEmail+ will be scheduled for
  # automatic incineration at a later point.
  #
  # When working with an +InboundEmail+, you'll usually interact with the parsed version of the source,
  # which is available as a +Mail+ object from +#mail+. But you can also access the raw source directly
  # using the +#source+ method.
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  #   inbound_email.mail.from # => 'david@loudthinking.com'
  #   inbound_email.source # Returns the full rfc822 source of the email as text
  class InboundEmail < Record
    include Incineratable, MessageId, Routable

    has_one_attached :raw_email, service: ActionMailbox.storage_service
    enum :status, %i[ pending processing delivered failed bounced ]

    def mail
      @mail ||= Mail.from_source(source)
    end

    def source
      @source ||= raw_email.download
    end

    def processed?
      delivered? || failed? || bounced?
    end

    def instrumentation_payload # :nodoc:
      {
        id: id,
        message_id: message_id,
        status: status
      }
    end
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# The +Message-ID+ as specified by rfc822 is supposed to be a unique identifier for that individual email.
# That makes it an ideal tracking token for debugging and forensics, just like +X-Request-Id+ does for
# web request.
#
# If an inbound email does not, against the rfc822 mandate, specify a Message-ID, one will be generated
# using the approach from +Mail::MessageIdField+.
module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::MessageId
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    # Create a new +InboundEmail+ from the raw +source+ of the email, which is uploaded as an Active Storage
    # attachment called +raw_email+. Before the upload, extract the Message-ID from the +source+ and set
    # it as an attribute on the new +InboundEmail+.
    def create_and_extract_message_id!(source, **options)
      message_checksum = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(source)
      message_id = extract_message_id(source) || generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)

      create! raw_email: create_and_upload_raw_email!(source),
        message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum, **options
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      nil
    end

    private
      def extract_message_id(source)
        Mail.from_source(source).message_id rescue nil
      end

      def generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)
        Mail::MessageIdField.new("<#{message_checksum}@#{::Socket.gethostname}.mail>").message_id.tap do |message_id|
          logger.warn "Message-ID couldn't be parsed or is missing. Generated a new Message-ID: #{message_id}"
        end
      end

      def create_and_upload_raw_email!(source)
        ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload! io: StringIO.new(source), filename: "message.eml", content_type: "message/rfc822",
                                               service_name: ActionMailbox.storage_service
      end
  end
end

**Deconstructing the Message-ID Deduplication Challenge**

Okay, so I'm looking closely at ActionMailbox's implementation, specifically the database migration and the `inbound_email/message_id.rb` file. The built-in uniqueness index on `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` is on `[:message_id, :message_checksum]`, which isn't just a simple `message_id` constraint. This is because if an *exact* duplicate raw email comes through, both the `message_id` and the `message_checksum` are the same, and the system gracefully handles the `RecordNotUnique` error, essentially discarding the duplicate. Makes sense.

However, the problem is that if the `Message-ID` stays the same but the raw email body *changes* (perhaps due to retries with added headers like `Received`, or whitespace differences, or changed `Delivered-To`), the `message_checksum` will be different. This means ActionMailbox's default setup *would* allow a second entry with the same `message_id`.

Now, considering the requirement: "Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry." This means two things:

1.  If an email with a specific `Message-ID` has already been processed and considered *valid* (i.e., successfully created a ticket, added a comment, or otherwise marked as processed), any subsequent email with the *same* `Message-ID` (even if the checksum differs) *must* be ignored. No duplicates.
2.  If an email with a `Message-ID` (say `<abc@example.com>`) is *invalid* (fails validation, bad headers, issues during processing, or if it isn't parsed properly) it *cannot* block a later, valid retry with the same `Message-ID`.

I'm thinking, what *makes* a delivery invalid? HTTP-level errors (authentication, wrong content type) are one thing, but what about malformed email bodies, missing fields (`From`, `To`, `Subject`, `Body`) or issues during processing after the `InboundEmail` object is created? If we blindly record `message_id` on the first encounter, an invalid delivery *could* block a retry.

Here's the scenario: an email with `<123@example.com>` arrives with invalid data (e.g. blank body or subject). It errors, but if we've already stored `<123@example.com>` in a unique index, then a later, valid delivery with the *same* `Message-ID` (e.g., corrected headers/body, retry) would be blocked. That's a huge issue.

The solution is to only record the `Message-ID` as processed when the delivery is *actually valid*. This means waiting to store a processed `Message-ID` until the ticket or comment is successfully created. We could use a dedicated table, column, or a status indicator of some kind, as long as that record only exists for *valid* deliveries. In that case, the invalid delivery isn't marked as processed.

Now, let's revisit ActionMailbox's built-in `[:message_id, :message_checksum]` index. If we have the *exact* same email (same `message_id` and same `message_checksum`) retried *after* a previous invalid attempt, it'll still be discarded, but it would have been dropped at the mail server, which is still a problem, especially for transient errors. If the retry is *valid*, the checksum *will* be different (since the raw bytes are different), unless the problem was external (e.g. account didn't exist, customer suspended), in which case the `message_checksum` *will* be the same! It'll return `nil` on retry with the exact same bytes, and the retry is silently dropped!

Consider this: an email with `<retry@example.test>` is sent to `acme@support.example.test` *before* the account exists. If the *exact same* email is retried, and ActionMailbox has its built-in `[:message_id, :message_checksum]` index, that first failed attempt will *block* the retry, returning a 204. That's a problem, and the check that prevents the invalid delivery from blocking the valid delivery has to be higher up.

This way it avoids creating a user if the associated ticket or comment fails validation; we don't want to create orphaned or half-baked accounts or the possibility of sending emails for things that don't exist.

**Deduplication and Email Replies: A Deep Dive**

Okay, let's break this down. First, the plan is to keep `serialize_ticket` and `serialize_request` untouched, because we don't need breaking changes. The idea of keeping compatibility is key. However, if the `origin` is actually helpful for later analysis, it's worth considering it. The email reply address, `reply_address`, is handled privately in email headers, so no changes are needed here.

Now, let's think about email replies. The system only allows the requester to reply. If they do, the following happens:
*   The system checks that `sender_email` matches `ticket.requester.email` (case-insensitive and normalized), and that the requester and the account are active.
*   If another customer, staff member, or unknown email sends an email, it MUST be ignored. Don't create anything new: no comment, no new tickets, and no new users.
*   Replying by email won't verify a user's account; `ticket.requester.verified_at` stays `nil`.
*   A valid reply creates a `Comment` on the `ticket` with `author: ticket.requester`, `body: plain_text_body`, and `public: true`.
*   The ticket status changes to "open" if it was "pending" or "solved."
*   If the ticket is already "open," it stays that way.
*   Replies don't send emails back to the customer, unless the original ticket came via email.

Also, it is important to generate a `reply_token` on *every* ticket, even if it's not email-originated. It's harmless, and it provides a consistent private reply address regardless of the ticket's origin.

Let's switch gears and focus on deduplication by `Message-ID` and handling invalid deliveries. This is super important! The goal is to make sure an invalid delivery doesn't block later, valid retries. Here's a quick walkthrough of how `ActionMailbox` works: `create_and_extract_message_id!` is the function that does the heavy lifting. It creates the `InboundEmail` model with a unique index on `[:message_id, :message_checksum]`.

Now, here's how to think about all the possible scenarios:

*   **Scenario 1:** Duplicate `Message-ID`, different raw source. This will create a duplicate `InboundEmail` record, and without deduplication, it could create a duplicate ticket or comment.
*   **Scenario 2:** Duplicate `Message-ID`, same raw source, after a valid delivery. The unique index in `ActionMailbox` will catch this, and no duplicate ticket or comment will be created.
*   **Scenario 3:** Invalid delivery followed by a valid retry with the same `Message-ID`. The first delivery MUST NOT create a ticket/comment/user, and MUST NOT be recorded. A later retry should go through!
*   **Scenario 4:** Invalid delivery, then the exact same raw email is retried. If the initial `InboundEmail` record is in the `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` table (due to an invalid delivery), the unique index will prevent a retry from *ever* being routed! This is a *problem*.

To solve the Scenario 4 problem, we can use a `inbound_email_receipts` (or `processed_messages`) table with a unique index on `message_id`, combined with a partial unique index on the `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` table. In `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` the partial index should be `WHERE status IN (0, 1, 2)`, so that it only applies to `pending`, `processing`, or `delivered` emails. In this table/column, only the `message_id` is stored.

This way, if an email is invalid (`bounced` or `failed`), it won't block a later valid retry, even of the exact same raw email, because it won't be in the index.

We will insert into the `inbound_email_receipts` table (with the unique `message_id`) *only when* the email has a `Message-ID` header. If an email *doesn't* have a `Message-ID`, `ActionMailbox` generates one from `message_checksum`, but different emails without `Message-ID` will have different checksums and won't get deduplicated against each other.

  # Encapsulates a route, which can then be matched against an inbound_email and provide a lookup of the matching

**Action Mailbox Implementation Strategy**

Okay, this is exciting! Seeing that `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` in `routes` is set up confirms we're on the right track with Action Mailbox. The plan is clear: I need to update the core models (`Account`, `Ticket`, `InboundEmailReceipt`), build out the mailer (`TicketMailer`) and its associated views, make the necessary adjustments to the `TicketsController`, and then create `ApplicationMailbox` and the specific `SupportMailbox`.

Let me quickly review `Account` to ensure I'm up to date: The relationships look good – `has_many :tickets`, `has_many :inbound_email_receipts`, etc., plus the `support_domain` and `support_address` methods. The current use of `ENV` is as expected.

Now, let's take a look at `Ticket` to be completely thorough: The validations, normalizations, and associations are all consistent with the design. The reply token generation using `SecureRandom.hex(16)` is standard practice. Also, the defined methods, such as `email_origin?` and `reply_address`, seem properly designed.

Checking the `InboundEmailReceipt` model is essential: the `belongs_to` associations and the uniqueness validation on `message_id` look correct.

I am now thinking about the `SupportMailbox` implementation! Let me trace a nuanced edge case: What about message ID case-sensitivity? Specifically, would `<foo@bar.test>` and `<FOO@bar.test>` be treated differently? Need to dive into RFC 5322 and see what Action Mailbox's handling is. Ah, Action Mailbox stores `mail.message_id` as-is, which is good.

I'm also considering the potential for issues with extremely long `Message-ID` values. Given PostgreSQL's lack of a specific character limit for `string` columns (as defined in Rails migrations!), that's probably not an immediate concern.

However, how does `mail.recipients_addresses` behave when it encounters an invalid `To:` header format, like `To: ""` or `To: undisclosed-recipients:;`? I should probably run a quick test in Ruby to confirm the behavior in these specific cases. This will inform how robust the parsing in the Mailbox needs to be.

    From: avery@example.test
    To: undisclosed-recipients:;
    Cc: acme@support.example.test
    Subject: Group test

    Hello
  MAIL

  p recipients: m.recipients_addresses.map(&:address)
'

**Refining the Inbound Email Handling**

Okay, so `Mail.from_source` and `recipients_addresses` are working cleanly to filter out the "undisclosed-recipients:;" header and grab the target address, in this case `["acme@support.example.test"]`. Good.

But wait, what about those Action Mailbox headers? I need to check how `X-Original-To` or `X-Forwarded-To` are handled. Let me look at `lib/action_mailbox/mail_ext/addresses.rb`. Okay, so `x_original_to_addresses` uses `Mail::Address.new`, which could raise `Mail::Field::IncompleteParseError` if the header syntax is bad. Right, right! So in `SupportMailbox`, I'll wrap `support_recipient_addresses` with safe, header-by-header parsing, catching `Mail::Field::ParseError`. That prevents malformed optional headers from crashing the whole thing with a 500 error, which would be terrible!

Now, let's consider another scenario: What if the `To` header already has `acme@support.example.test`, AND either `X-Original-To` or `Delivered-To` *also* has `acme@support.example.test`? Well, it should resolve to the same `account` ("acme"), so `businesses.uniq(&:id)` will be size 1, no problem.

Okay, next. What if the `From` address is tricky, like a customer with a display name that has quotes or UTF-8 encoded characters? Let's say something like `From: =?UTF-8?B?Sm9zw6k=?= <jose@example.test>`. Ah! The `Mail` gem automatically decodes `from_addr.display_name` to `"José"`! Perfect! And what about the `Subject` line? Like, say, `Subject: =?UTF-8?B?SGVsbG8gY2Fmw6k=?=`. The `mail.subject` should auto-decode it to `"Hello café"`! Nice! And just to be super safe, I should still encode the `subject` to UTF-8 before using it, just in case, using `to_utf8(mail.subject).strip`.

cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > app/models/account.rb
class Account < ApplicationRecord
  CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD = 90.days

  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :inbound_email_receipts, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false },
            format: { with: /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/ }

  def self.support_domain
    ENV.fetch("HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN", "support.example.test").to_s.strip.downcase.presence || "support.example.test"
  end

  def support_address
    "#{subdomain}@#{self.class.support_domain}"
  end

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def within_reactivation_window?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && cancelled_at >= at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
  end

  def cancellation_expired?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && !within_reactivation_window?(at: at)
  end

  def cancel!(at: Time.current)

require "securerandom"

class SupportMailbox < ActionMailbox::Base
  LIST_HEADERS = %w[
    List-Id
    List-Unsubscribe
    List-Post
    List-Help
    List-Subscribe
    List-Owner
    List-Archive
    Mailing-List
  ].freeze

  AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS = %w[
    X-Autoreply
    X-Autorespond
    X-Auto-Reply
    X-Failed-Recipients
  ].freeze

  AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE_VALUES = %w[bulk list junk auto_reply autoreply].freeze
  AUTOMATED_LOCAL_PARTS = %w[
    mailer-daemon
    postmaster
    noreply
    no-reply
    do-not-reply
    donotreply
  ].freeze

  def process
    if already_processed?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if automated_or_list_mail?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    sender = extract_sender
    if sender.nil?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    body_text = extract_plain_text_body
    if body_text.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    target = resolve_target
    if target.nil?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    account = target[:account]
    ticket = target[:ticket]

    if account.cancelled?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if ticket
      process_reply(account:, ticket:, sender:, body_text:)
    else
      process_new_ticket(account:, sender:, body_text:)
    end
  end

  private

  def already_processed?
    InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
  end

  def automated_or_list_mail?
    auto_submitted = header_value("Auto-Submitted")
    return true if auto_submitted.present? && auto_submitted.downcase != "no"

    precedence = header_value("Precedence") || header_value("X-Precedence")
    return true if precedence.present? && AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE_VALUES.include?(precedence.downcase)

    return true if LIST_HEADERS.any? { |name| header_value(name).present? }
    return true if AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS.any? { |name| header_value(name).present? }

    suppress = header_value("X-Auto-Response-Suppress")
    return true if suppress.present? && suppress.downcase.match?(/\b(all|oof|autoreply)\b/)

    if mail.header["Return-Path"].present? && mail.return_path.blank?
      return true
    end

    return true if mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase == "multipart/report"

    from_addr = extract_from_addresses.first
    if from_addr&.local.present? && AUTOMATED_LOCAL_PARTS.include?(from_addr.local.to_s.strip.downcase)
      return true
    end

    false
  end

  def header_value(name)
    field = mail.header[name]
    return nil if field.nil?

    Array(field).first&.value.to_s.strip.presence
  end

  def extract_from_addresses
    field = mail.header[:from]
    return [] if field.nil?

    el = field.respond_to?(:element) ? field.element : field.address_list
    Array(el&.addresses)
  rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
    []
  end

  def extract_sender
    addresses = extract_from_addresses
    return nil unless addresses.size == 1

    from_addr = addresses.first
    email = from_addr.address.to_s.strip.downcase
    return nil unless email.match?(URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP)
    return nil if from_addr.domain.to_s.strip.downcase == Account.support_domain

    raw_name = from_addr.display_name.presence || from_addr.name.presence || email.split("@").first
    name = to_utf8(raw_name).strip.presence || email.split("@").first

    { email: email, name: name }
  end

  def extract_plain_text_body
    raw_text = if mail.text_part
                 decode_part(mail.text_part)
               elsif !mail.multipart? && mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase != "text/html"
                 decode_part(mail)
               elsif mail.html_part
                 ActionView::Base.full_sanitizer.sanitize(decode_part(mail.html_part))
               elsif !mail.multipart? && mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase == "text/html"
                 ActionView::Base.full_sanitizer.sanitize(decode_part(mail))
               end

    raw_text.to_s.gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
  end

  def decode_part(part)
    decoded = part.decoded
    charset = part.charset
    to_utf8(decoded, charset)
  rescue Mail::Field::ParseError, Encoding::UndefinedConversionError, Encoding::InvalidByteSequenceError
    to_utf8(part.body.raw_source)
  end

  def to_utf8(str, charset = nil)
    return "" if str.nil?

    text = str.to_s.dup
    if text.encoding == Encoding::ASCII_8BIT && charset.present?
      enc = Encoding.find(charset) rescue nil
      text.force_encoding(enc) if enc

  end

  def collect_recipient_addresses
    addresses = []

    %i[to cc bcc].each do |header_name|

    %w[x_original_to x_forwarded_to delivered_to].each do |header_name|
      Array(mail.header[header_name]).each do |field|
        list = Mail::AddressList.new(field.to_s)
        addresses.concat(Array(list.addresses))
      rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
        next
      end
    end

    addresses
  end

  def resolve_target
    support_domain = Account.support_domain
    support_addrs = collect_recipient_addresses.select do |addr|
      addr.domain.to_s.strip.downcase == support_domain
    end
    return nil if support_addrs.empty?

    plain_subdomains = []
    reply_pairs = []

    support_addrs.each do |addr|
      local = addr.local.to_s.strip.downcase
      next if local.blank?

      if local.include?("+")
        subdomain, token = local.split("+", 2)
        return nil if subdomain.blank? || token.blank?

        reply_pairs << [ subdomain, token ]
      else
        plain_subdomains << local
      end
    end

    plain_accounts = plain_subdomains.empty? ? [] : Account.where(subdomain: plain_subdomains.uniq).to_a

    reply_tickets = []
    reply_pairs.uniq.each do |subdomain, token|
      ticket = Ticket.joins(:account).includes(:account, :requester).find_by(
        reply_token: token,
        accounts: { subdomain: subdomain }
      )
      return nil if ticket.nil?

      reply_tickets << ticket
    end

    businesses = (plain_accounts + reply_tickets.map(&:account)).uniq(&:id)
    return nil unless businesses.size == 1

    unique_tickets = reply_tickets.uniq(&:id)
    return nil if unique_tickets.size > 1

    { account: businesses.first, ticket: unique_tickets.first }
  end

  def process_reply(account:, ticket:, sender:, body_text:)
    unless ticket.requester.email == sender[:email]
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if ticket.requester.suspended?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      comment = ticket.comments.create!(
        author: ticket.requester,
        body: body_text,
        public: true
      )
      if %w[pending solved].include?(ticket.status)
        ticket.update!(status: "open")
      end
      InboundEmailReceipt.create!(
        message_id: inbound_email.message_id,
        account: account,
        ticket: ticket,
        comment: comment
      )
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    bounced!
  end

  def process_new_ticket(account:, sender:, body_text:)
    subject = to_utf8(mail.subject).strip
    if subject.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    verification_token = nil
    requester = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      account.lock!

      existing_user = account.users.find_by(email: sender[:email])
      if existing_user
        if existing_user.suspended?
          bounced!
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end
        requester = existing_user
      else
        requester = account.users.create!(
          name: sender[:name],
          email: sender[:email],
          password: SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32),
          role: "customer"
        )
        verification_token = requester.issue_email_verification_token!
      end

      ticket = account.tickets.create!(
        requester: requester,
        subject: subject,
        status: "open",
        origin: "email"
      )
      comment = ticket.comments.create!(
        author: requester,
        body: body_text,
        public: true
      )
      InboundEmailReceipt.create!(
        message_id: inbound_email.message_id,
        account: account,
        ticket: ticket,
        comment: comment
      )
    end

    return if inbound_email.bounced?

    if verification_token.present?
      UserMailer.email_verification(requester, verification_token).deliver_now
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    bounced!
  end
end

**Aha! I've Got It! The Test Suite is Tripping Up on Incineration!**

Okay, so I see the error: `NotImplementedError: Use a queueing backend to enqueue jobs in the future`. Remember that head-scratcher we had earlier with `IncinerationJob` and its `set(wait: 30.days).perform_later` call, especially when using `:inline` as the queue adapter?

This is it! `ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::InlineAdapter#enqueue_at` is the culprit. It explicitly raises that `NotImplementedError`, which explains why the test is failing.  Action Mailbox's `Incineratable` is the trigger, specifically when `inbound_email.delivered!` or `inbound_email.bounced!` is called. It schedules the `ActionMailbox::IncinerationJob` using `set(wait: 30.days).perform_later(self)`.

I *knew* that `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false` in `config/environments/test.rb` was there for a reason! It's preventing the `after_update_commit :incinerate_later` callback from even *trying* to call `enqueue_at` on the `:inline` adapter!  That's the standard Rails fix for this issue.

Now, what about `development` or `production`? Would someone using `:inline` or `:async` have a problem there?  In those environments, the default is `:async`, which *does* support `enqueue_at`, so it's all good. But in `test`, because we're using `:inline`, we *need* that `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false` setting to prevent the error.

Alright, let's add that `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false` to `config/environments/test.rb`, and let's rerun the test suite. Problem solved, I'm sure!

messages.thinking:
**Expanding the Email Support Testing**

Okay, so the current test suite runs with 34 runs, 972 assertions, zero failures, errors or skips - that's a good start. But I need to dive deeper and cover *every* possible edge case to ensure the system's robustness. Let's make sure these email workflows are solid.

First, I need to really consider those email edge cases. What happens when the subject is blank? I need to test that a ticket shouldn't be created, and the customer shouldn't be created, and the verification email is not sent, and then the retry with the correct subject *succeeds*. Similarly, what if the `From` header is invalid or missing? Again, no ticket or user, and the retry MUST work.

Then, what about those situations where multiple businesses are involved (To and Cc)? An invalid first attempt shouldn't block a valid retry later. We need to test that.

I have to thoroughly think through a complete email flow: customer opens a ticket via email, gets verified, resets password, signs in to the portal, sees the ticket, replies, and then a staff member replies – and verify that the whole flow works properly.

Next, I need to test UTF-8 characters and encoding (quoted-printable, base64) in the subject, From display name, and body. Gotta cover all those character sets! And what about the `Message-ID`? Test uppercase/lowercase, and missing angle brackets. We need to handle variations properly.

I'm also going to check what happens if `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD` isn't set, and someone still tries to use the endpoint. ActionMailbox should raise an `ArgumentError`.

Wait, there are more considerations. For the `TicketMailer.staff_reply`, does it correctly prevent "Re: Re: " when replying? Yep. Good!

And what about a suspended customer? If they email, the system should ignore it – no ticket or comment. Make sure the logic is correct!

Finally, I need to test the interaction between `Account.purge_expired_cancellations!` and email-origin tickets/`InboundEmailReceipt`s, and make sure that `on_delete: :cascade` handles things gracefully.

And one final thing: I will make sure the unit tests using `ActionMailbox::TestCase` are using our `SupportMailbox` correctly.

All of these new scenarios need to be added as integration tests in `test/integration/email_support_test.rb`. Then, let's run all tests to ensure the system is rock solid.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat <<'EOF' >> test/integration/email_support_test.rb

EOF
ruby -e '
  path = "test/integration/email_support_test.rb"
  content = File.read(path)
  extra_tests = <<~RUBY

  test "blank subject, invalid sender, and multi-business invalid deliveries do not block later valid retries" do
    # Blank subject -> ignored, does not block retry with same Message-ID
    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "sara@example.test",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      subject: "   ",
      body: "Body without subject",
      message_id: "<blank-subj@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 0, @acme.tickets.count
    assert_nil @acme.users.find_by(email: "sara@example.test")

    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "sara@example.test",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      subject: "Now has subject",
      body: "Body with subject",
      message_id: "<blank-subj@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 1, @acme.tickets.count
    assert_equal "Now has subject", @acme.tickets.first.subject

    # Invalid From -> ignored, does not block retry with same Message-ID
    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "not-a-valid-email",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      subject: "Bad sender",
      body: "Body",
      message_id: "<bad-from@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 1, @acme.tickets.count

    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "valid-sender@example.test",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      subject: "Valid sender retry",
      body: "Body",
      message_id: "<bad-from@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 2, @acme.tickets.count

    # Multi-business -> ignored, does not block single-business retry with same Message-ID
    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "multi-retry@example.test",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      cc: "beta@support.example.test",
      subject: "Multi biz",
      body: "Body",
      message_id: "<multi-retry@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 2, @acme.tickets.count

    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "multi-retry@example.test",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      subject: "Single biz retry",
      body: "Body",
      message_id: "<multi-retry@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 3, @acme.tickets.count
  end

  test "email-origin customer can verify, reset password, use portal, and purge cascades receipts" do
    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "=?UTF-8?B?Sm9zw6k=?= <jose@example.test>",
      to: "acme@support.example.test",
      subject: "=?UTF-8?B?Q2Fmw6kgaXNzdWU=?=",
      body: "Need help with café order",
      message_id: "<portal-e2e@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content

    jose = @acme.users.find_by!(email: "jose@example.test")
    assert_equal "José", jose.name
    ticket = @acme.tickets.first
    assert_equal "Café issue", ticket.subject
    assert_equal "Need help with café order", ticket.comments.first.body

    verify_token = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last)
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear

    # Unverified cannot sign in yet; confirm verification
    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
         params: { email_verification: { token: verify_token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert jose.reload.verified?

    # Set password via password reset to access portal
    post "/api/v1/password_resets",
         params: { password_reset: { email: "jose@example.test" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    reset_token = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last)

    post "/api/v1/password_resets/confirm",
         params: { password_reset: { token: reset_token, password: "jose-new-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    jose_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "jose@example.test", password: "jose-new-password")
    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: auth_headers("acme", jose_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ticket.id ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    # Suspended user cannot open tickets or reply via email
    jose.update!(suspended: true)
    post_relay build_raw_email(
      from: "jose@example.test",
      to: ticket.reply_address,
      subject: "Re: Café issue",
      body: "Suspended reply",
      message_id: "<suspended-reply@example.test>"
    )
    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal 1, ticket.comments.count

    # Purging expired cancelled account cascades inbound_email_receipts
    @acme.cancel!(at: 91.days.ago)
    Account.purge_expired_cancellations!
    assert_nil Account.find_by(id: @acme.id)
    assert_equal 0, InboundEmailReceipt.where(account_id: @acme.id).count
  end
  RUBY

  updated = content.sub(/\n  private\n/, "\n#{extra_tests}\n  private\n")
  File.write(path, updated)
' && DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_test?host=/var/lib/postgresql" bin/rails test
